reviewedRevision: 62ccd0c plus the rework in this commit
process: Lean final review at the user's request: the known 3-level shortfall went straight to a retrofit, followed by one independent review round. Its one MEDIUM finding (input dropped during animation locks) and a level 16 tuning note were fixed and verified by re-running the reviewer's own probes, one clean-worktree run and the browser check, without a second review round.
independentProbes: The reviewer modelled human memory: over 20 seeds per level, a good player (about 14 cards) cleared 398 of 400 level runs, an average player (9 cards, 5% misremembering) 358, a weak player (6 cards) 269, and a pure guesser 44, almost all on the unlimited-leaf levels 1 and 2. A perfect-memory bot with a 0.25 s or 0.35 s decision delay cleared 200 of 200 with most of the clock left. Blind patterns won at most 1.5% from level 3. On the final files the reviewer's average player cleared 368 of 400 (level 16 rose from 4 to 14 of 20), and its lock probe showed three correct Echo taps at 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 s cadence all registering with no leaf lost. The clock never runs during an animation; progress stores, fuzz, determinism at 30, 60 and 120 Hz and EN/ZH text fit all passed.

findings.observation: Only 3 levels with 3 rule types and no select or continue. There are now 20 data-driven clearings mixing pairs, a numbered lantern route, triples and a new Echo rule (repeat a growing lit sequence), with leaves, optional previews and a between-turns decision clock, ten distinct card shapes plus check, cross and step-number cues, accurate EN/ZH tips, a clearing select and env.progress continue; the 695-line file is split into seven modules.

Review finding: taps and keys during card animations were silently dropped, so tapping a remembered Echo sequence at a natural pace lost a step and then a leaf. Up to two taps or Space presses now queue during a lock and apply the moment play is ready, arrow keys always move the cursor, and a correct Echo entry locks for 0.15 s instead of 0.35 s.

Review tuning note: Long Lantern Trail (level 16) cleared 4 of 20 for an average memory. It now has a 6 s preview, 21 leaves and a 140 s clock; average players clear it 14 of 20 and weak players 3 of 20.

openNotes: Leaf budgets on the triples and pairs mastery levels are generous: a player remembering half the cards clears levels 15 and 19 most of the time.
Human limits on an 8-cue Echo at 0.5 s per cue and on 10-pair previews are estimates from simulated memory, not playtests.
Levels 1 and 2 have unlimited leaves, so they cannot be lost.

browser.method: Official Claude in Chrome extension, local server; real clicks on Start and the cards, synthetic in-page keys; only DOM text and the canvas were read.
observed: Chinese: Start opened clearing 1 of 20 (蕨叶初见) with a 2.1 s preview of three pairs, unlimited leaves and no clock.
Win: after the preview, flipping the remembered pairs (figures, trees, mushrooms) matched all three in three turns with check marks; the clearing showed 3/3, score 570 and a Next button.
Chinese 390 px phone frame (388 px inner, no horizontal overflow): six touch buttons (向左 向右 向上 向下 翻牌/下一关 休闲); the clearing select showed clearing 1 cleared and clearing 2 unlocked after the win.
Not covered in the browser: a loss and the Echo rule, which start from clearing 3 and 6; the reviewer's players and the quality tests cover them.
